## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to isolate environments using environment-specific backend keys and to configure CI so QA changes never impact production or development environments. It also validates practical drift-detection steps and proper CIDR planning for network isolation.

## Key Concepts
- Backend isolation using `-backend-config`
- Per-environment var-files and resource scoping
- Drift detection with `-detailed-exitcode`
- CI pipeline gating for QA-only operations

## Code Example
```bash
terraform init -backend-config="path=envs/qa/terraform.tfstate" -reconfigure
terraform plan -var-file=envs/qa.tfvars -detailed-exitcode
terraform apply -var-file=envs/qa.tfvars -auto-approve
```

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical drift remediation techniques on large multi-resource deployments, emphasizing targeted changes and plan-deduplication.

## Key Concepts
- Drift detection via plan exit codes
- Resource tainting vs. full apply
- Targeted applies to minimize blast radius
- For_each resource addressing

terraform init
terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -out=tfplan
# identify address from plan output, e.g. aws_subnet.env["subnet-0a1b2c"]

terraform apply -auto-approve -target='aws_subnet.env["subnet-0a1b2c"]'
terraform plan
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you automate this across all drifted resources in a single run?
- How do you ensure idempotence when using -target in CI pipelines?

## Why This Is Asked

# Verify no drift
terraform plan
```

Why This Is Asked
Tests backend aliasing, per-env isolation, and plan validation via JSON to ensure QA never touches prod.
